messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2059007777 - inference-queue growth detected for customer-prod-1. queue_length=870, oldest_request=00:04:12, latency_p50=420ms, throttled=true
Alex Chen: seeing the alert, jumping in. which cluster/zone is this hitting?
Maya O.: looks like us-east-1a dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-3). Autoscaler logs show attempted scale but failed due to placement constraints.
Priya Singh: confirmed. autoscaler: attempt=3, desired=12, launched=0, reason=PLACEMENT_FAILED_FRAGMENTATION.
Tom B.: oh no, MIG slices mismatch again? we recently changed MIG profile on that pool to 1g.
Alex Chen: any recent deployments or config changes to nodegroups there?
sre-rotation: @alex @maya no config change in k8s nodegroup for that pool in last 24h. But infra did an instance refresh yesterday (mix of A100 and A10g).
Maya O.: snippet from scheduler: "unable to pack pods: insufficient contiguous gpu-slice: need 2x1g contiguous, available non-contiguous single-gpu-slices=6"
Priya Singh: TL;DR: fragmented MIG allocations are leaving stranded capacity. autoscaler respects MIG topology so it won't launch pods that won't binpack. queue just keeps growing.
Alex Chen: what's the customer impact? which customers on that pool?
Maya O.: customer-prod-1 & background embedding batch jobs. prod requests are getting 429s from the frontend when queue exceeds threshold. CS flagged one ticket: "generation requests failing intermittently".
Tom B.: immediate mitigations? can we fallback to hosted pool or lower-MIG granularity model?
Priya Singh: options: 1) emergency rebalance (drain some nodes, re-create with aligned MIG sizes), 2) provision fallback on hosted (latency increase), 3) temporarily allow multi-slice packing override (dangerous).
Alex Chen: we need fast mitigation with minimal customer impact. Priya, what's fastest?
Priya Singh: fastest is failover to hosted fallback model for prod routing—apply routing rule to route requests to model-variant:cpu-fallback or hosted-gpu-fallback. That buys time while we rebalance.
Maya O.: I can flip the route, but need approval from oncall lead. @sre-rotation can you authorize?
sre-rotation: authorized. Flip it. :white_check_mark:
Maya O.: doing now. updating route: 
```
redwood-cli routes update --route prod-generation --fallback hosted:rw-medium --wait
```
Maya O.: route updated. traffic 90% -> hosted fallback, 10% -> dedicated (canary).
Alex Chen: monitor error rates and latency. set alerts for >5% 500s on hosted.
Priya Singh: initiating node rebalance plan: mark 4 nodes unschedulable in pool, cordon+drain, delete, recreate with MIG profile 2x1g contiguous slices to reduce fragmentation. This is heavy.
Tom B.: how long to recreate nodes? ~8-12 mins per node incl. instance warmup + runtime. We should do parallel replacements by 2 at a time.
Maya O.: creating a runbook snippet in thread for ops: 
```
- cordon node <n>
- drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- delete node from ASG
- create instance with MIG profile=2x1g
- wait for kube-ready + inference runtime healthy
- uncordon
```
Priya Singh: starting cordon for node-07 and node-12 now.
Alex Chen: logs show some pods stuck in PENDING with scheduling failure: "Insufficient contiguous gpumemory: requested 2x1g contiguous, available fragments: 1g@node-05, 1g@node-09". That explains stranded capacity.
Maya O.: also seeing autoscaler hitting cloud quota for launching new instances? There was a transient limit error: "quota_exceeded: vgpu-instances 10/10" in cloud provider logs. That prevented autoscaler from attempting different instance types.
Priya Singh: noted. I requested quota bump to cloud but that's slow. Rebalance is still our primary fix.
Tom B.: while we rebalance, hosted fallback is serving most requests. CS noted latency increase ~200ms p50 but errors dropped.
Alex Chen: assign tasks: Maya perform route & monitoring (done), Priya handle node rebalance, Tom liaise with CS & customer to inform they might see slower responses but no failures, Alex coordinate handoff and postmortem.
Maya O.: update: node-07 cordoned, drain complete, deleting instance. Node recreated with MIG 2x1g, kube-ready at +9m. Placing pods back.
Priya Singh: node-12 started cordon. Starting replacement in parallel with node-09 (2 at a time).
Tom B.: CS message prepared: "We detected a capacity fragmentation issue causing retries; we've routed traffic to a fallback pool and are rebalancing capacity. Expect slight latency increase; errors resolved." Sending now.
Alex Chen: any signs of further queue growth?
Maya O.: queue length dropped to 120 after route flip + first node replacement. Throttled=false. CPU & GPU utilization normalized on dedicated pool.
Priya Singh: continuing replacements until fragmentation reduced below threshold. Will monitor autoscaler behavior; may re-enable direct routing slowly.
sre-rotation: reminder to update incident page and tag SLO owners.
Alex Chen: oncall handoff at 08:00 UTC — @sre-rotation to take next shift. Document what we did and outstanding items.
Maya O.: creating incident ticket INC-2059 with timeline and mitigation steps. Adding links to logs and runbook.
Tom B.: follow-up actions: 1) add automated MIG packing check in scheduler (alert when fragmentation > 30%), 2) add quick-failover route for production models, 3) request cloud quota bump and pre-warm instance pool for major customers.
Priya Singh: agreed. Also schedule a short postmortem to decide whether to change default MIG profiles for the pool.
Alex Chen: thanks all. handing off to @sre-rotation. leaving this thread open for async updates. :thumbsup:
